slides.say: For every number x, diamond of x is x to the power of five, plus three x to the power of four, minus two x cubed, plus x squared, plus four x, minus seven. Diamond of two minus diamond of negative two is equal to what?

slides: A long rule, and we need its value at two minus its value at negative two. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, calculating both values, and then a shortcut with even and odd powers.

slides.say: [short pause] Diamond of two first. Two to the power of five is thirty-two. Two to the power of four is sixteen, and three times sixteen is forty-eight. Two cubed is eight, and two times eight is sixteen, with a minus. Two squared is four. Four times two is eight. And minus seven. Now add them step by step. Thirty-two plus forty-eight is eighty. Eighty minus sixteen is sixty-four. Sixty-four plus four is sixty-eight. Sixty-eight plus eight is seventy-six. Seventy-six minus seven is sixty-nine.

Now diamond of negative two. An odd power of a negative number stays negative, and an even power becomes positive. So negative two to the power of five is negative thirty-two. Negative two to the power of four is sixteen, and three times sixteen is forty-eight. Negative two cubed is negative eight, and minus two times negative eight is plus sixteen. Negative two squared is four. Four times negative two is negative eight. And minus seven.

Negative thirty-two plus forty-eight is sixteen. Sixteen plus sixteen is thirty-two. Thirty-two plus four is thirty-six. Thirty-six minus eight is twenty-eight. Twenty-eight minus seven is twenty-one. So sixty-nine minus twenty-one is forty-eight. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to compare each term at two and at negative two, instead of calculating everything. An even power gives the same value for two and for negative two. The plain number, minus seven, is also the same. So in the subtraction, all of these cancel.

An odd power changes only its sign. For example, two cubed is eight, and negative two cubed is negative eight. Eight minus negative eight is sixteen, which is twice eight. So every term with an odd power of x counts twice its value at two.

So we keep only the terms with an odd power of x, and double their values at two. Those terms are x to the power of five, minus two x cubed, and four x, which has x to the power of one. Their coefficients stay. At two, that's thirty-two minus sixteen plus eight, which is twenty-four. Twice twenty-four is forty-eight. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
